metaTitle: Best Throw Blankets for Couches in 2026
metaDescription: Six throw blankets for couches compared on size, fabric weight, texture and washing care, so you can pick a throw that is warm, soft and easy to live with.
expertTake: The Bedsure reversible sherpa fleece throw is the top pick because it combines a smooth fleece face with a thick, warm pile in a washable polyester. The Bedsure lightweight fleece is the value pick for year round use. Skip a faux fur throw if you have pets that shed or you dislike a blanket that sheds for the first few washes.
introParagraphs: A throw blanket does two jobs at once: it keeps you warm on the sofa and it adds a layer of texture to a living room. The wrong one is either too thin to be cozy or so bulky that it never gets used.

The details that decide it are size, fabric type, weight and how the blanket behaves after a few washes. Pilling, shedding and static are the quiet disappointments of cheap fleece, so care matters as much as feel.

products.name: Bedsure GentleSoft Reversible Sherpa Fleece Throw Blanket for Couch
products.description:
Bedsure's sherpa fleece throw is a reversible blanket with a smooth fleece side and a fuzzy sherpa side. The listing describes it as thick and warm, and it carries a note that it is non heated, so it relies on trapping body heat rather than any wiring. The two sides give you a smooth look for decor and a cozy side for use.

Sherpa is the better match for a living room in cold weather, because the pile traps air. Compared with the Bedsure lightweight fleece, it is heavier and warmer but also harder to wash and dry. Compared with the faux fur version, the sherpa sheds less and matts less.

Wash it on a gentle cycle in cold water with similar fabrics, and tumble dry on low. Avoid fabric softener, which coats the fibers and reduces fluff. For a sofa that gets used every evening, it is the most balanced choice here. Fold it in thirds over the sofa arm when you are not using it, and the reversible sides give two looks.
products.bestFor: Cold evenings on the sofa where warmth and a reversible look both matter.
pros: Looks tidy folded on a sofa arm
cons: Heavier to wash and dry than light fleece
Sherpa pile can collect pet hair

products.name: UGG Bliss Fleece Throw Blanket 50 x 70 Inch, Charcoal Grey
products.description:
UGG's Bliss throw measures 50 by 70 inches, which is 10 inches longer than a standard lap throw and enough to cover a seated adult from shoulders to feet. The fabric is a reversible plush fleece in charcoal grey, and the listing mentions an Oeko Tek certification.

The extra length makes it a more practical throw for stretching out on a sofa. Compared with the Bedsure sherpa, it is a smoother, more refined fleece and less bulky, but it is also less warm. The charcoal color pairs with gray and navy sofas.

An Oeko Tek mark means the textile was screened for harmful substances, but it does not say anything about pilling. Wash it cold and dry low. It suits a modern living room where the throw is part of the styling. On a large sofa, the 70 inch length also lets you tuck one end under a cushion so it stays in place.
products.bestFor: Stretching out on the sofa with a throw that reaches the feet.
pros: 50 by 70 inch size covers a seated adult
cons: Less warm than a sherpa pile
Dark color shows pet hair and lint

products.name: PU MEI Reversible Sherpa Fleece Throw 60 x 80 Inch, Lattice Pattern

specList.label: Pattern
specList.value: Staggered grid in gray, cream and soft blue

products.description:
PU MEI states its fabric weights: one side is 240 GSM soft flannel and the other is 230 GSM sherpa. A stated weight is rare in this category and lets you compare it with other throws. The size is 60 by 80 inches, which is large enough for two people or to drape over a sofa.

The lattice pattern in gray, cream and soft blue is a bolder look than the plain colors. Compared with the Bedsure sherpa, it is larger and patterned, and each layer is mid weight, so the blanket feels substantial but not stiff.

Because it is oversized, it needs more room in the washer, so use a large drum and low heat. It is a good choice for a family sofa where two people share a blanket. If you have a sectional, drape it over the chaise so that both people can reach it.
products.bestFor: Two people sharing a sofa or draping over a sectional.
cons: Large size needs a big washer

products.name: Bedsure Faux Fur Fluffy Sherpa Throw 50 x 60 Inch, Grey

specList.label: Pile
specList.value: 1.5 in shaggy plush on one side

products.description:
Bedsure's faux fur throw pairs a 1.5 inch shaggy plush face with a sherpa fleece back. At 50 by 60 inches it is a standard lap size. The listing describes it as thick and warm while balancing warmth and weight.

Faux fur is the most decorative option in this group, with a deep pile that reads as luxury on a sofa. Compared with the plain Bedsure sherpa, it is more dramatic but sheds more and traps more pet hair, and the long pile can mat if washed hot.

Wash it on gentle cold and tumble dry on the lowest setting. Shake it out before first use, because it will shed fibers. Choose it for a styled living room, not a pet heavy household. Use a wide tooth comb to refluff the pile after washing, which keeps it from matting.
products.bestFor: Styled living rooms that want a dramatic, textured throw.
cons: Sheds fibers and traps pet hair
Long pile can mat if dried hot

products.name: L'AGRATY Chunky Knit Chenille Throw Blanket 50 x 60 Inch, Ivory
products.description:
L'AGRATY offers a chunky knit chenille throw in ivory, 50 by 60 inches. The thick, textured stitches make it a decor piece as much as a blanket. The listing describes it as handmade crochet chenille.

A knit throw is more of a visual element than a warm blanket, because the open stitches let heat escape. Compared with the sherpa throws, it is lighter and breathes better, but it will not feel as snug on a cold evening.

Chunky knits snag on jewelry and pet claws, so keep it away from rough surfaces. Wash gently or hand wash and lay flat to dry to avoid stretching. It is the best choice for a neutral, textured living room. A basket beside the sofa shows it off when it is not in use.
products.bestFor: Textured, neutral rooms where the throw is part of the styling.
pros: Looks good draped over a chair

products.name: Bedsure Lightweight Flannel Fleece Throw Blanket, Grey
products.description:
Bedsure's flannel fleece throw is the lightweight option, described as thicker and softer than the classic version while staying airy. It is a versatile blanket for the couch, bed or travel. The grey color is neutral.

Light fleece is the easiest to care for: it dries fast, resists pilling better than cheap microfiber and does not shed like faux fur. Compared with the sherpa throw, it is cooler and less bulky, so it suits a warm climate or a year round blanket.

Wash it cold and dry low to prevent pilling. It is the best value in the group. Because it is light, it travels well and folds small for a car or a cabin.
products.bestFor: Year round use and easy care at a lower tier.
pros: Resists shedding better than faux fur

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 50 by 60 inch throw is a lap size. A 50 by 70 inch throw, like the UGG Bliss, covers a seated adult from shoulders to feet. A 60 by 80 inch throw, like the PU MEI, suits two people. Choose the size by how you will use it, not by how it looks folded. If you are tall, add 10 inches in length rather than width, because feet are what stick out. A throw that reaches only your lap is fine for a chair, but a sofa nap wants the longer size.

Flannel fleece is light and easy to wash, sherpa is warm and bulky and faux fur is decorative and sheds. Chenille knits, like the L'AGRATY, are textured and breathable. Match the fabric to your climate and your cleaning habits. A blend of fabrics, such as a flannel face with a sherpa back, gives a clean look and a cozy feel. Chunky knits are mostly decorative, so pair one with a warmer fleece throw if you want both looks.

GSM shows fabric weight. The PU MEI lists 240 and 230 GSM layers, which is mid weight. A light fleece feels cooler than a thick faux fur. Weight and warmth are related but not identical. If you run warm, pick a lighter GSM, because a thick pile can trap heat.

Faux fur and sherpa shed in the first washes, and polyester fleece pills over time. Wash inside out on cold and avoid fabric softener. A tighter weave sheds less. Wash a new throw once before use, because loose fibers come out and the feel improves.

Most polyester throws are machine washable, but chenille and chunky knits need gentle care. Heat mats faux fur. Check the label and use low heat. Many pet owners keep a dedicated throw on the sofa so that hair stays off the main blankets.

Neutral grey, cream and ivory suit most sofas. A pattern like the PU MEI's lattice adds texture. Dark colors show lint and pet hair. A color that is one shade away from your sofa looks calm and styled. If the room is busy with patterns, a solid color throw calms the look.

specDecoder.meaning: GSM is grams per square meter and shows fabric weight. Higher numbers are heavier and usually warmer.
specDecoder.watchFor: The PU MEI lists 240 GSM flannel and 230 GSM sherpa, which is a mid weight pair.

specDecoder.meaning: Sherpa is a fleece with a fuzzy pile that imitates wool lining. It traps air and feels warm but bulky.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bedsure GentleSoft and PU MEI use sherpa backs, so expect more shedding than plain fleece.

specDecoder.meaning: Faux fur is a deep pile synthetic fabric. It looks luxurious but sheds and mats when heated.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Bedsure faux fur lists a 1.5 inch pile, so dry it on the lowest setting.

specDecoder.meaning: Chenille is a soft, fuzzy yarn often used for chunky knits. Knits are open and breathable but snag easily.
specDecoder.watchFor: The L'AGRATY is chenille, so keep it away from jewelry and pet claws.

specDecoder.meaning: Oeko Tek Standard 100 means the textile was screened for harmful substances. It does not measure softness or durability.
specDecoder.watchFor: The UGG Bliss lists it, but pilling is still possible after many washes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fabric and feel
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared flannel fleece, sherpa, faux fur and knit based on the spec sheet and the fabric descriptions. The Bedsure sherpa and PU MEI combine a smooth face with a pile back, while the L'AGRATY is a pure knit. Feel is subjective, so we weighted fabric type and weight over adjectives.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared sizes against real use. The UGG Bliss at 50 by 70 inches and the PU MEI at 60 by 80 inches cover more than the 50 by 60 inch throws. A blanket that actually covers you is more likely to be used.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warmth and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the stated weights and pile depth. The PU MEI lists 240 and 230 GSM layers, and the Bedsure faux fur has a 1.5 inch pile. Warmth and bulk are related but not the same.

howWeEvaluated.title: Care and durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered shedding, pilling and washing. Faux fur and sherpa shed, light fleece dries fast and knits need gentle care. A throw that stays soft after many washes earned more credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Look and fit with decor
howWeEvaluated.description: We judged color, pattern and texture against typical living rooms. The ivory knit and grey fleece suit neutral rooms, while the lattice pattern adds texture. Owner feedback patterns informed our caution on pet hair and lint.

cards.label: Sherpa
cards.text: The Bedsure GentleSoft and PU MEI have a fuzzy pile that traps air. They are warm and bulky, and they shed in the first washes.

cards.label: Flannel fleece
cards.text: The Bedsure lightweight fleece is thinner and airy. It dries fast, resists shedding better and suits year round use, but it is less cozy in deep winter.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A tight weave that sheds little, a smooth face and a color that hides hair. Avoid long pile faux fur and open knits that catch claws. Check that it is machine washable.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Bedsure lightweight fleece and the UGG Bliss fit best, because their smooth surfaces release hair when shaken or brushed. Skip the faux fur and knit throws.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a larger size or a refined fleece that looks styled. The UGG Bliss and PU MEI cover more of you and look more finished.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a simple warm blanket for daily use. The Bedsure fleece and faux fur cost less and cover the need.

maintenance.why: Body oils and skin cells collect in the pile. Wash on a gentle cold cycle with similar fabrics.
Shaking removes dust and lifts the pile. A quick tumble with a dryer ball on air restores fluff.
Bound edges can loosen over time. Re stitch small gaps before they spread.
A lint roller or damp rubber glove lifts hair from fleece. Brush faux fur gently.
Hang the throw outside or near an open window. This removes odors without a wash.

faq.q: What size throw blanket should I buy?
faq.a: A 50 by 60 inch throw is a lap size. A 50 by 70 inch throw covers a seated adult, and a 60 by 80 inch throw suits two people. Choose based on how you use it. If you are buying as a gift, a 50 by 60 inch throw is the safest size.

faq.q: Is sherpa or fleece better for a couch throw?
faq.a: Sherpa is warmer and bulkier, and it suits winter. Flannel fleece is lighter and easier to wash. Choose sherpa for cold rooms and fleece for year round use. A throw with a fleece face and a sherpa back gives you both in one blanket.

faq.q: Why do faux fur throws shed?
faq.a: New faux fur has loose fibers from the cutting process, and they come out in the first washes. Shake it before use and wash on cold. Shedding eases after a few cycles. A sticky roller or a damp cloth lifts loose fibers faster than shaking.

faq.q: How do I wash a throw blanket without damaging it?
faq.a: Wash on a gentle cold cycle with similar fabrics, and avoid fabric softener. Tumble dry on low or air dry. High heat mats the pile and shortens the life. A mesh laundry bag also protects knit throws from the drum.

faq.q: Why does my fleece throw pill?
faq.a: Pilling happens when short fibers rub and form small balls. It is more common after hot washes and rough fabrics. A fabric shaver removes pills.

faq.q: How do I stop static in a polyester throw?
faq.a: Static comes from dry air and polyester. Add a humidifier in winter or tumble with a wool dryer ball. Avoid dryer sheets, which coat the fibers. A small amount of fabric softener is not worth the loss of fluff.
